title: Is Claude my contract's lawyer?
text: People type it like this, is Claude my contracts lawyer? It isn't. It's my contracts checklist, the same steps every single time. So, what does that checklist actually catch and what does it miss? People hand Claude a contract expecting a review. What actually runs in between is a written file, skill.md.

title: The natural guess — read it all, weigh it, decide
text: The natural assumption, Claude reads it like a lawyer would, weighing the whole document clause by clause, case by case.

title: A skill is a folder, not a judgment call
text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. Skill.md is the whole instruction set, plain language, no hidden logic. The pipeline is fixed, read the file, execute each step in order, return the result. Linear, no branching unless a step says so. So, it isn't judgment, it's a checklist written in advance. That trade buys repeatable results, the same input gets the same output every run.

title: The anchor — a freelance contract, flagged
text: Run it on a freelance contract and it flags the termination clause. The checklist says, look there, so it looks. But, the checklist only names what it names. An arbitration clause the list never mentions gets no comment, not because it's fine.

title: The anchor returns — same flag, not a verdict
text: Run the same contract again, the termination flag comes back identical. That's consistency, a flag means a listed check matched, not a verdict on the contract. And a clean pass isn't a clean bill of health, either. It means nothing on the list tripped. What's off the list stays invisible, either way. A

title: Carry-out
text: Skill.md gives Claude the same checklist every time, that's consistency, not judgment. So, the read through is still yours.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn, paste this into Claude along with any contract you're reviewing. Before you review this, list exactly what you will check for and what you will not. Then do the review. That first list turns an invisible checklist into one you can see.

title: Outro
text: Claude contract review, the checklist, not the lawyer. Liam in for Bear.
